A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Toward Relative Positional Encoding in Spiking Transformers. Their main text, figures, tables, proofs, appendices, and checklists support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: V2 reports original forecasting, text classification, image classification, sensitivity, and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds forecasting comparisons in Table 1 and runtime and GPU-memory measurements in Table 5.

M1.justification: XNOR attention, Gray-Code concatenation, Log-PE biases, and two-dimensional Gray-PE remain unchanged. Spikingformer provides another evaluation backbone. The new hardware discussion describes implementation possibilities without establishing a changed experimental or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four forecasting datasets, six short-text benchmarks, AGNEWS and IMDB, and four image-classification benchmarks. The new efficiency comparison reuses Electricity; no new data population or task scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Transformer-with-ALiBi and Spikformer-with-ALiBi comparisons, plus Spikingformer without PE and its Gray-PE/Log-PE variants. Existing forecasting comparators and the classification comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New Section 5.6 evaluates seconds per epoch and GPU memory on Electricity with prediction horizon 24. This adds a resource-measurement protocol; retained experiments preserve their stated splits, sequence lengths, metrics, and Appendix D training settings.

E4.justification: Table 5 newly investigates the computational overhead of XNOR relative to original Spikformer and CPG-PE. The Gray-Code bit-width sensitivity analysis in Figure 3 and the XNOR/Log-PE ablations in Table S1 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains three-seed averaging, Table 2 retains five-seed means and standard deviations, and Tables 3/S2 retain four-seed averaging. V3 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds ALiBi scores and Spikingformer results: average R² is 0.693 without PE, 0.711 with Gray-PE, and 0.716 with Log-PE. New Table 5 reports original/XNOR runtime of 137.48/139.66 seconds per epoch and memory of 10572.56/10608.32 MB. Matched results in Tables 1–4, S1–S2, and Figure 3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Gray-Code theorem and Appendix A proof are unchanged. New Appendix E adds a limited analytical storage-cost estimate, K(N+2P) bits, for a K-interval piecewise-linear lookup table with N-bit inputs and P-bit parameters.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about binary-compatible approximate RPE, the Gray-Code property, two-dimensional encoding, and improvements across architectures and tasks.

C2.justification: Section 5.6 and Appendix E add substantive arguments about XNOR hardware compatibility and avoiding runtime logarithms through precomputation or lookup tables. Existing result interpretations and limitations remain, with limitations moved from Appendix E to F.

D1.justification: V3 adds guidance on bitwise tensor operations, offline bias storage, and optional lookup-table implementation. Its abstract explicitly identifies the previously linked SeqSNN repository as the paper's code, although the checklist retains future-release wording. Existing hyperparameters and hardware descriptions are unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to Spikingformer, Loihi, and TrueNorth for the expanded comparison and hardware discussion. Existing citations and the central positioning relative to prior positional-encoding methods are retained.

P1.justification: V3 expands the RoPE background, inserts an efficiency section and hardware appendix, moves Broader Impact before the references, and adds acknowledgments. Affiliation and conference text are updated; most existing prose and narrative organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains rows and corrects SDT-V1 with Log-PE from absolute to relative PE; Table 5 is new. Figure 2 explicitly inserts Gray-Code mappings into its distance labels. Other figures and tables retain their displays apart from placement and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The added ALiBi and Spikingformer comparisons strengthen support for existing claims, while Table 5 supplies concrete GPU-cost evidence absent from v2. The retained results and theory are preserved. Broader neuromorphic-efficiency claims remain argued rather than experimentally demonstrated, so the overall improvement is limited.
